..(Thursday night through Tuesday)
Issued at 505 AM EDT WED AUG 5 2026

The latest model data indicates that the forecast remains on track
for a rather wet start to the extended period followed by less 
storm coverage but also potential for organized activity as the 
upper levels become more favorable. The diurnal cycle should 
dominate the timing of the convection each day into the start of 
the weekend. Later, impulses aloft will have their say in 
initiating convection, but the timing and placement of these 
elements remain fraught with uncertainty. 

The previous long term discussion follows:

Active weather continues into the long term period, with daily 
chances for showers and storms in the forecast grids. Expect the 
greatest precipitation coverage during the first half of the 
forecast period, when a more favorable troughing pattern will be in 
place over the Ohio River Valley and Greater Midwest. A series of 
shortwave impulses moving through this broader troughing will 
bolster late-week rain chances across the commonwealth, and recent 
forecast guidance suggests that a better-defined disturbance will 
dig into the commonwealth in the Friday to Saturday time frame. The 
resultant increase in forcing could allow more locations to 
experience measurable rainfall on these dates. Likewise, relatively 
higher amounts of shear could allow those week-end showers/storms to 
organize beyond the typical summertime pop-up archetype. However, 
the intensity of any late-week activity is largely conditional upon 
that parent disturbance aligning with the diurnal instability cycle. 
Such timing details remain highly uncertain, and there is not enough 
forecast confidence to delineate any severe weather risks in this 
time frame. 

There is much higher confidence in the forecast for multiple rounds 
of heavy rainfall across portions of Eastern Kentucky through the
end of the week. Highs in the mid to upper 80s and dewpoints in 
the 70s will pose favorable thermodynamics for convective lift on 
Thursday, Friday, and Saturday afternoon. Ensemble data continues 
to resolve 1500-2000+ J/kg of CAPE across Eastern Kentucky during 
peak diurnal heating. Mean soundings around the region depict very
little CIN alongside high freezing levels (above 15k feet) and 
cloud-layer winds in the 10-15 knot range. Given all of the above 
and PWATs in the 1.7-1.9" range, the thunderstorms that develop 
later this week are poised to be slow-moving and efficient 
rainmakers. Even if the previously-discussed shortwave 
disturbances arrive at night and storms are unable to take 
advantage of peak diurnal instability, the repetitive rainfall 
could prove excessive. Isolated instances of flash flooding cannot
be ruled out if any given location experiences multiple downpours
in the same day or if slow-moving storms track over the same 
places multiple days in a row. To cover this risk, WPC has 
delineated a series of Marginal (Level 1/4) Excessive Rainfall 
Outlooks across the entire JKL CWA for these three days. 

Forecast confidence decreases next week, but this morning's forecast 
guidance continued the trend towards a drier early-week forecast. 
The latest data collectively resolves midlevel height rises and weak 
quasi-zonal flow over the Ohio River Valley for Sunday, Monday, and 
Tuesday. This is in response to the amplification of a ridge across 
the Southwestern and Central CONUS, although there is still some 
uncertainty regarding its eastern extent. If a stronger ridge 
emerges, temperatures could bump up in our forecast area. For now 
though, the forecast calls for climatologically appropriate 
thermometer readings. Expect highs in the mid/upper 80s and lows in 
the 60s/near 70s, albeit with less moisture than earlier in the 
period. Ensemble mean PWATs decrease to between 1.4-1.6" next week, 
largely due to the advection of a drier continental airmass in the 
midlevels. The late-period PoPs are largely modulated by the diurnal 
heating cycle. There could still be isolated to scattered summertime 
pop-ups, but barring any ridge-riding shortwave support, the late-
period showers and storms should be fairly mundane. In short, the 
forecast area is in store for typical summertime sensible weather 
next week.
